To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lower-class individuals experience more hostile emotion in social interactions and are more vigilant to threats of hostility.
lower class rank, whether measured by objective social class or subjective social class, is associated with increased vigilance for threat and increased reactivity to hostile emotion.
social class rank shapes the experience and perception of hostility in social situations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how social class rank shapes emotional reactivity to interpersonal hostility.
the way in which perceived class rank shapes social interactions, and the implications of class-based hostile reactivity for the perpetuation of class-based social inequalities.
how class-based differences in vigilance to social threat shape social interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lower-class individuals are more vigilant to social threat relative to their high ranking upper-class counterparts.
social class rank, because of its effect on the vigilance to social threat and hostile reactivity, affects the emotional content of human interaction.
the lower the socioeconomic class of a person, the more they experience hostile emotions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
class-related vigilance for threats can shape social interactions, and the effects of class are likely a function of both class rank and class-based differences in socialization and social support.
lower-class individuals experience more hostility than upper-class individuals in social interactions.
class rank shapes the social experience by leading individuals to experience more threat in social situations, especially in the form of hostility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the class-based social threat hypothesis is a viable and useful theoretical approach for understanding the role of class in social life.
the social class of individuals is an important predictor of social perception and emotion.
the class-based threat vigilance is a mechanism by which social class shapes social interaction and human emotion.
